parameters.name: ad_user
parameters.description: Active Directory username. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: adfs_authority_url
parameters.description: Azure AD authority url. Use when authenticating with Username/password, and has your own ADFS authority.

parameters.name: api_profile
parameters.description: Selects an API profile to use when communicating with Azure services. Default value of latest is appropriate for public clouds; future values will allow use with Azure Stack. Default: "latest"

parameters.name: append_tags
parameters.description: Use to control if tags field is canonical or just appends to existing tags. When canonical, any tags not found in the tags parameter will be removed from the object’s metadata. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: auth_source
parameters.description: Controls the source of the credentials to use for authentication. Can also be set via the ANSIBLE_AZURE_AUTH_SOURCE environment variable. When set to auto (the default) the precedence is module parameters -> env -> credential_file -> cli. When set to env, the credentials will be read from the environment variables When set to credential_file, it will read the profile from ~/.azure/credentials. When set to cli, the credentials will be sources from the Azure CLI profile. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if more than one is present otherwise the default az cli subscription is used. When set to msi, the host machine must be an azure resource with an enabled MSI extension. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if the resource is granted access to more than one subscription, otherwise the first subscription is chosen. The msi was added in Ansible 2.6. Choices: "auto" ← (default) "cli" "credential_file" "env" "msi"

parameters.name: cert_data
parameters.description: Aan existing valid certificate, containing a private key, into Azure Key Vault.

parameters.name: cert_validation_mode
parameters.description: Controls the certificate validation behavior for Azure endpoints. By default, all modules will validate the server certificate, but when an HTTPS proxy is in use, or against Azure Stack, it may be necessary to disable this behavior by passing ignore. Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CERT_VALIDATION environment variable. Choices: "ignore" "validate"

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Azure client ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal or Managed Identity (msi). Can also be set via the AZURE_CLIENT_ID environment variable.

parameters.name: cloud_environment
parameters.description: For cloud environments other than the US public cloud, the environment name (as defined by Azure Python SDK, eg, AzureChinaCloud, AzureUSGovernment), or a metadata discovery endpoint URL (required for Azure Stack). Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT environment variable. Default: "AzureCloud"

parameters.name: disable_instance_discovery
parameters.description: Determines whether or not instance discovery is performed when attempting to authenticate. Setting this to true will completely disable both instance discovery and authority validation. This functionality is intended for use in scenarios where the metadata endpoint cannot be reached such as in private clouds or Azure Stack. The process of instance discovery entails retrieving authority metadata from https://login.microsoft.com/ to validate the authority. By setting this to **True**, the validation of the authority is disabled. As a result, it is crucial to ensure that the configured authority host is valid and trustworthy. Set via credential file profile or the AZURE_DISABLE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY environment variable. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the certificate is enabled for use. Choices: false true

parameters.name: log_mode
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: log_path
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Certificate name.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: If the private key in the passed in certificate is encrypted, it is the password used for encryption.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.description: The management policy for the certificate. When generating a new certificate, if no policy is set, the default policy will be used.

parameters.name: certificate_transparency
parameters.description: Indicates if the certificates generated under this policy should be published to certificate transparency logs. Choices: false true

parameters.name: certificate_type
parameters.description: Type of certificate to be requested from the issuer provider.

parameters.name: content_type
parameters.description: he media type (MIME type) of the secret backing the certificate. Choices: "application/x-pkcs12" ← (default) "application/x-pem-file"

parameters.name: enhanced_key_usage
parameters.description: The extended ways the key of the certificate can be used.

parameters.name: exportable
parameters.description: Indicates if the private key can be exported. For valid values, see KeyType. Choices: false true

parameters.name: issuer_name
parameters.description: Name of the referenced issuer object or reserved names. For example self and unknown. Choices: "self" "unknown"

parameters.name: key_curve_name
parameters.description: Elliptic curve name. For valid values, see KeyCurveName. Choices: "P-256" "P-384" "P-521" "P-256K"

parameters.name: key_size
parameters.description: The key size in bits. For example 2048, 3072, or 4096 for RSA.

parameters.name: key_type
parameters.description: The type of key pair to be used for the certificate. Choices: "EC" "EC-HSM" "RSA" "RSA-HSM" "oct" "oct-HSM"

parameters.name: key_usage
parameters.description: The extended ways the key of the certificate can be used. Choices: "digitalSignature" "nonRepudiation" "keyEncipherment" "dataEncipherment" "keyAgreement" "keyCertSign" "cRLSign" "encipherOnly" "decipherOnly"

parameters.name: lifetime_actions
parameters.description: Actions that will be performed by Key Vault over the lifetime of a certificate.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The type of the action. Choices: "EmailContacts" "AutoRenew"

parameters.name: days_before_expiry
parameters.description: Days before expiry to attempt renewal. Value should be between 1 and `validity_in_months` multiplied by 27. If validity_in_months is 36, then value should be between 1 and 972 (36 * 27).

parameters.name: lifetime_percentage
parameters.description: Percentage of lifetime at which to trigger. Value should be between 1 and 99.

parameters.name: reuse_key
parameters.description: Indicates if the same key pair will be used on certificate renewal. Choices: false true

parameters.name: san_dns_names
parameters.description: Subject alternative DNS names of the X509 object. Either subject or one of the subject alternative name parameters are required for creating a certificate.

parameters.name: san_emails
parameters.description: Subject alternative emails of the X509 object. Either subject or one of the subject alternative name parameters are required for creating a certificate.

parameters.name: san_user_principal_names
parameters.description: Subject alternative user principal names of the X509 object. Either subject or one of the subject alternative name parameters are required for creating a certificate.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The subject name of the certificate. Should be a valid X509 distinguished name. Either subject or one of the subject alternative name parameters are required for creating a certificate. This will be ignored when importing a certificate; the subject will be parsed from the imported certificate.

parameters.name: validity_in_months
parameters.description: The duration that the certificate is valid in months.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Security profile found in ~/.azure/credentials file.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: Azure client secret. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State of the keyvault certificate. Choices: "generate" "import" "delete" "purge" "recover" "merge" "update"

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: Your Azure subscription Id.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Dictionary of string:string pairs to assign as metadata to the object. Metadata tags on the object will be updated with any provided values. To remove tags set append_tags option to false. Currently, Azure DNS zones and Traffic Manager services also don’t allow the use of spaces in the tag. Azure Front Door doesn’t support the use of Azure Automation and Azure CDN only support 15 tags on resources.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: Azure tenant ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: thumbprint
parameters.description: The thumbprint of the private key specified in x509_certificate_path. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal. Required if x509_certificate_path is defined.

parameters.name: vault_uri
parameters.description: Vault uri where the certificate stored in.

parameters.name: x509_certificate_path
parameters.description: Path to the X509 certificate used to create the service principal in PEM format. The certificate must be appended to the private key. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

examples:
- name: Import a keyvault certificate
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    enabled: true
    password: Password@****
    cert_data: "{{ lookup('file', 'cert.pem') }}"
    state: import
    tags:
      key1: value1

- name: Generate a keyvault certificate
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    policy:
      subject: 'CN=Anhui02'
      issuer_name: self
      exportable: true
      key_type: RSA
      key_size: 2048
      san_emails:
        - 7170222076@qq.com
      content_type: 'application/x-pkcs12'
      validity_in_months: 36
      lifetime_actions:
        - action: EmailContacts
          days_before_expiry: 10
    enabled: true
    state: generate

- name: Rotate Key Vault Certificate with a renewed PEM bundle
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    cert_data: "{{ lookup('file', 'new_cert.pem') }}" # PEM must include private key + cert
    policy:
      content_type: "application/x-pem-file"
    state: import

- name: Rotate Key Vault Certificate with a renewed PFX bundle
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    cert_data: "{{ lookup('file', 'new_cert.pfx') | b64encode }}" # PFX must include private key + cert
    password: Password@****
    policy:
      content_type: "application/x-pkcs12"
    state: import

- name: Update the keyvault certificate
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    policy:
      subject: 'CN=Anhui'
      issuer_name: self
      exportable: true
      key_type: RSA
      key_size: 2048
      san_emails:
        - 7170222076@qq.com
      content_type: 'application/x-pkcs12'
      validity_in_months: 36
      lifetime_actions:
        - action: EmailContacts
          days_before_expiry: 10
    enabled: true
    state: update

- name: Purge the keyvault certificate
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    state: purge

- name: Recover the keyvault certificate
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    state: recover

- name: Delete the keyvault certificate
  azure_rm_keyvaultcertificate:
    vault_uri: https://vault{{ rpfx }}.vault.azure.net
    name: fredcerticate
    state: absent

return_values.name: certificates
return_values.description: The facts of certificates in Azure Key Vault. Returned: always

return_values.name: cert_data
return_values.description: CER contents of the X509 certificate. Returned: always Sample: "MIID*****************0pRjXE"

return_values.name: deleted_on
return_values.description: The time when the certificate was deleted, in UTC. Returned: always Sample: "2025-01-14T09\""

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: The name of the certificate. Returned: always Sample: "testcert"

return_values.name: policy
return_values.description: The management policy of the deleted certificate. Returned: always

return_values.name: attributes
return_values.description: Certificate attributes. Returned: always

return_values.name: created
return_values.description: Creation datetime. Returned: always Sample: "2025-01-14T09:41:20+00:00"

return_values.name: enabled
return_values.description: Indicate whether the certificate is enabled. Returned: always Sample: "True"

return_values.name: expires
return_values.description: Expiration datetime. Returned: success Sample: "None"

return_values.name: not_before
return_values.description: Not before datetime. Returned: success Sample: "None"

return_values.name: recoverable_days
return_values.description: Reflects the deletion recovery days. Returned: always Sample: "None"

return_values.name: recovery_level
return_values.description: Reflects the deletion recovery level currently in effect for certificates in the current vault. If it contains ‘Purgeable’ the certificate can be permanently deleted by a privileged user, Otherwise, only the system can purge the certificate, at the end of the retention interval. Returned: always Sample: "None"

return_values.name: updated
return_values.description: Update datetime. Returned: always Sample: "2025-01-15T09:41:20+00:00"

return_values.name: certificate_transparency
return_values.description: Indicates if the certificates generated under this policy should be published to certificate transparency logs. Returned: always Sample: "None"

return_values.name: certificate_type
return_values.description: Type of certificate to be requested from the issuer provider. Returned: str Sample: "None"

return_values.name: content_type
return_values.description: If not specified, the media type (MIME type) of the secret backing the certificate. Returned: always Sample: "application/x-pkcs12"

return_values.name: enhanced_key_usage
return_values.description: The extended ways the key of the certificate can be used. Returned: always Sample: ["1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1", "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2"]

return_values.name: exportable
return_values.description: Indicates if the private key can be exported. Returned: always Sample: true

return_values.name: issuer_name

return_values.name: key_curve_name

return_values.name: key_size

return_values.name: key_type

return_values.name: reuse_key

return_values.name: san_dns_names
